A first-pass checklist, US-oriented. Rules differ by country and state; ask a local accountant or lawyer before you commit.

<span id="choose-how-you-will-operate"></span>
== 1. Choose how you will operate ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Option
! Good for
! Watch for
|-
| Informal collective or sole proprietor
| Volunteer work, no money moving
| Personal liability; cannot easily receive grants; no tax deductibility for donors
|-
| LLC or similar company
| Selling services or products around the commons
| You pay tax on profit; does not make donations tax-deductible
|-
| Non-profit corporation, then tax-exempt status
| A funded organization in its own right
| Set-up cost, annual filings, governance rules, months of waiting for approval
|-
| Project of a fiscal sponsor
| Taking grants and deductible donations without your own entity
| A fee, and the sponsor’s rules; see [[Fiscal sponsorship]]
|}

<span id="get-the-basics-in-place"></span>
== 2. Get the basics in place ==

* A legal name and a registered entity if you chose one
* A tax ID (in the US, an EIN from the IRS, which is free)
* A separate bank account, never your personal one
* Simple bookkeeping from day one: every receipt and every payment categorized
* A written record of who decided what (the [[Decision log]] is a start)

<span id="protect-the-open-source-commons"></span>
== 3. Protect the open source commons ==

* Keep the licence on your forks and respect each project’s contribution policy.
* Do not use vendor names or logos as your own branding. Names may be used only to describe compatibility.
* Keep your work inside the clean-room rules (see [[Rules of the road]]).
